notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White plates in both short and long sizes, often mixed; the only Latin American country to do so.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Taxis and buses have older solid orange plates or newer ones with an orange bar on top.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 3 is a white car with a short thick antenna, not always visible.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 4 is a white pickup truck with a black trunk and no antenna.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A low-quality camera with a wide circular blur and brownish colours, sometimes a red logo at the front; unique in Latin America.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Very common bollards: a round one with two red stripes, and a flat one with two red reflectors on black.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Concrete poles with many small ladder-like indents are practically unique in Latin America; most other poles are round concrete.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Concrete roads are relatively common.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Double guardrails are used very commonly.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Lots of chevrons in curves, usually far more than elsewhere in Latin America.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Many square white road signs.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Green kilometre markers with the highway shield.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Sign backs are painted teal blue on thin metal posts; unique in Latin America.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: One-way signs have text inside the arrow, like in the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Most houses are grey brick with metal roofs, while Peru and Bolivia favour red brick.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Hexagonal tile paving in urban areas.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The first letter on a taxi or plate usually matches the province name.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The Andes run down the middle; east and west are flatter.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Banana plantations are most common in the southwest.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: An extremely dry landscape on the coast between Guayaquil and Manta.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat Amazon region with white-barked trees and oil palms, nearly all in high-antenna coverage.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Looks like the Amazon but significantly hillier.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Winding mountain roads and exposed brownish-red dirt in the southern regions.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Semi-arid with lots of pine trees.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: The high antenna variant is always in the northern half of the country.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles with oval see-through holes are most common in Loja province.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Guardrails in Guayas are often painted black and yellow.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Trekker and boat coverage only on the islands, with volcanic soil, low shrubs, craters and giant tortoises.
